{{Quote|Ataru is the name given to the movements of this form&mdash;though it is aggressive, it is focused, and its best use is in combat against a single opponent.|Zez-Kai Ell|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" />}}
'''Form IV''', also known as '''Ataru''', the '''Way of the Hawk-Bat''', or '''The Aggression Form''', was the fourth of the seven forms of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]]. The history of Ataru stretched back through the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]], to at least as early as the [[Mandalorian Wars]], where it was commonly employed by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] of that day. Ataru continued to be a common form among the Jedi in the latter stages of the Republic, and was also employed by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].

An aggressive style, Form IV was fast-paced and effective against single opponents, though weaker in prolonged combat and confined spaces. It was not recommended for use against opponents wielding [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]]. Ataru was characterized by [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-assisted acrobatics, such as somersaults and leaping strikes, both for attack and defense. Another characteristic of the form was its fast strikes from multiple directions. Notable users of this combat form during the Old Republic included [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]. The [[New Jedi Order]] preserved knowledge of Ataru, and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] such as [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Mara Jade Skywalker]], and [[Kyle Katarn]] employed it.

==Description==
{{Quote|Form IV, also called Ataru, is the most acrobatic Form, filled with numerous elaborate moves, and relies heavily upon a Jedi's ability to run, jump, and spin using the Force.|Cin Drallig|<ref name="EGTTF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Ewan.jpg|thumb|left|180px|The opening stance of Ataru]]
Ataru was an aggressive [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat]] form relying on a combination of speed and agility. Due to this, it was also called the Way of the [[Hawk-bat/Legends|Hawk-bat]] or the Aggression Form. Practitioners of Ataru were always on the offensive, attacking with wide and fast swings. Form IV practitioners constantly called upon [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to aid in their movements and attacks. By allowing the Force to flow throughout their body, they could [[Force valor|overcome their physical limitations]]&mdash;including old age, as was the case with [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]&mdash;and perform amazing feats of acrobatics, such as somersaults and backflips, not only for attack, but also to evade the slashes and strikes of their opponents.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> Jedi utilizing Ataru needed to incorporate all the [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] that involved surpassing normal physical ranges of motion, speed, and agility in order to be successful. Running, jumping, and spinning were all emphasized in learning the elaborate kinetics of the form.<ref name="EGTTF" />

Those who used Form IV could move at high speeds and could rain strong blows, jumping and attacking through the air. Powerful and quick spinning attacks could be utilized from all angles, either from ground or air. Masters of Ataru could appear like a blur to their opponents, attacking from all directions&mdash;the front, the sides, overhead, or behind. The Force not only allowed them to perform athletic feats impossible otherwise, but it also helped guide their actions and movements in combat.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" />

==Applications==
{{Quote|Against multiple enemies, only a true Ataru master will prevail.|Yoda|<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>}}
Ataru proved to be an effective combat form when used properly, and was common among Jedi during the [[Mandalorian Wars]]. It was well-suited to close combat, particularly against single opponents.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" /> Due to its speed and agility, Ataru was recommended for use by Jedi with the ability to [[Force speed/Legends|enhance their speed]] and stamina with the Force.<ref name="TJP" />

[[File:DotF_TPM.png|thumb|right|250px|Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi utilize Ataru against Darth Maul's Juyo on Naboo.]]
Because it was such an aggressive style, Ataru was not generally optimal against multiple opponents, and it was somewhat ineffective against [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire, particularly from multiple foes.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" /> Despite those weaknesses, [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] employed this form with great success during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] against numerous [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droids]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref> This form was also considered not as effective for prolonged combat, as the nature of Ataru could greatly tax the body. Ataru practitioners were advised to withdraw if they were unable to win after a devastating burst of Ataru attacks.<ref name="TJP" /> Fatigue was theorized to have been a contributing factor in Qui-Gon Jinn's defeat on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] at the hands of [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] during the latter stages of the Battle of Naboo. In fact, since their [[Duel on Tatooine/Legends|brief fight]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], Maul knew that Ataru would be the Jedi Master's undoing.<ref name="Journal Darth Maul">''[[Star Wars Journal: Darth Maul]]''</ref><ref name="Wrath of Darth Maul">''[[The Wrath of Darth Maul]]''</ref> Another contributing factor in Jinn's [[Death/Legends|death]] was the requirement of open space for the kinetic acrobatics of Ataru. Without ample space to move in the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]] [[Plasma Refinery Complex|reactor core]], Jinn was deprived of the key element in his defense, and thus could only attempt to block Maul's incessant barrage of [[Form VII/Legends|Form VII/Juyo]] strikes. This event influenced Kenobi&mdash;after his Master's death, he changed his preferred form to [[Form III/Legends|Form III/Soresu]], the most defensive of all forms.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" />

[[File:Ataru_Surprise_Hawk_Bat_Swoop_FDCR.png|thumb|left|200px|A female Jedi attacks an Emperor's Royal Guard using the Hawk Bat Swoop.]]
Through the Force, Yoda was considered to have mastered Form IV to its highest level. He used it in almost all of his battles, and his mastery of the style caused others to describe him as virtually unstoppable against most opponents, including Separatist battle droids, despite his small size and advanced age. His moves in his duel against [[Dooku/Legends|Count Dooku]] on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] were revealed on close examination to be a fast-paced demonstration of the standard components of Form IV. Each action flowed from one to another in the smooth transitions characteristic of Form IV. In addition, three kinds of rotation, called ''su ma'', figured prominently in his style: ''jung su ma'' (spinning), ''ton su ma'' (somersaults), and ''en su ma'' (cartwheels). These three moves represented the three possible axes of rotation in three-dimensional space. Together with [[Force jump/Legends|Force-enhanced jumps]], the rotational ''su ma'' moves composed most of his style, making the [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] exemplary of Form IV mastery.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> At one point prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Yoda gave demonstrations of the form in use, some of which were recorded on [[data book]]s in the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]].<ref name="EGTTF" /> Yoda also employed Ataru against the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] and [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] at the conclusion of the Clone Wars when [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|the Jedi Purge began]]. Despite its weaknesses to blaster fire and multiple opponents, Yoda's mastery of the form was such that he defeated the clones.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III: Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref>

Dooku stated that he understood "every weakness of the Ataru form, with its ridiculous acrobatics," given his many sparring sessions with Qui-Gon Jinn. Dooku's [[Form II/Legends|Form II]] would counter Ataru by launching a series of thrusts toward the enemy's legs to draw the opponent into a flipping overhead leap, so that Dooku could burn through the enemy's spine from kidneys to shoulder blades with his Makashi attack. The Count applied this tactic against Obi-Wan Kenobi, who blocked Dooku's blows with Soresu, on board the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']] during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith (novel)">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>

==Moves and maneuvers==
{{Quote|The Ataru form of combat is aggressive, but focused. You must never rely solely on skill with a weapon, but rather embrace the idea that your whole body is the weapon. Use the Force to spin, jump, to overpower your foe.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 1">[[Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 1|''Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost'' 1]]</ref>}}
[[File:Ataru_Striker_FDSS.png|thumb|right|200px|An Ataru practitioner makes an aggressive strike]]
The opening stance for Ataru was a balanced two-handed guard: holding the [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] vertically with both palms, either on the right or left side of the body.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith (novel)" /> One technique employed with greater effect by Ataru users was the Hawk-Bat Swoop. When utilized by Ataru practitioners, it was intended to allow a combatant to quickly strike their opponent without giving them a chance to react, and then escape before they had a chance to retaliate. Another move that Ataru users could use effectively was the Saber Swarm, where numerous short strikes were aimed at the adversary to force a defensive posture.<ref name="TJP" /> Ataru wielders were able to execute this combination with particular skill.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> Both the Hawk-Bat Swoop and the Saber Swarm were related to the [[Falling Leaf]] technique, and they gained in popularity during the [[New Sith Wars]].<ref name="TJP" />

==Practitioners==
{{Quote|This style of fighting was taught to me by Master Yoda. In most cases, you will not use it as a first resort, but you'll find it often works as a ''last'' resort.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 1" />}}
Besides Yoda and Qui-Gon Jinn, other notable practitioners of Ataru were Jedi Masters [[Tott Doneeta]],<ref name="JATM" /> [[Zez-Kai Ell]], [[Kavar]], [[Vrook Lamar]],<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" /> [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]],<ref name="The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> [[Cay Qel-Droma]],<ref name="JATM" /> [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]],<ref name="The Clone Wars Campaign Guide">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref> [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]],<ref name="TFU">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> [[Vandar Tokare]],<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> and [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]];<ref name="CWA: Ataru">{{TCWA|Lightsaber Duel}} {{C|Ataru Mastery Pack}}</ref> [[Battlemaster/Legends|Jedi Battlemasters]] [[Skarch Vaunk]]<ref name="TJP" /> and [[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]];<ref name="Order 66: Destroy All Jedi">{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}}</ref> Sith Lord Darth Maul;<ref name="Lockdown">''[[Maul: Lockdown]]''</ref> [[Sith Blademaster]] [[Kas'im]];<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" /> and [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Set Harth]].<ref name="DOE">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref> Some of Revan's [[Revanchist|Jedi Crusaders]] also practiced Ataru.<ref name="Fringe Stat Pack">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/FringeStatPack|text=Fringe Stat Pack}}</ref>

The Sith Lord [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]] used Ataru to defeat two [[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith acolytes]] of [[Darth Xedrix]] on [[Bosthirda/Legends|Bosthirda]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic: Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref> [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] and his [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]] also learned Ataru from Darth Tyranus.<ref name="Labyrinth of Evil">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>

Obi-Wan Kenobi had also mastered Ataru from his training by Qui-Gon Jinn, but after the death of his master on Naboo, Kenobi shifted to studying Soresu,<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> intent on creating a hybrid between it and Ataru to compensate for Ataru's lack of defense.<ref name="TJP" /> Although Soresu would become Kenobi's primary dueling form, he remained accomplished in Ataru and during the Clone Wars would often implement elements of Ataru, primarily its acrobatics, into his swordplay.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> When dueling Darth Tyranus on the ''Invisible Hand'' in the Battle of Coruscant, Kenobi started the duel using Ataru stances and techniques to mislead Tyranus.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith (novel)" />

[[File:AniTwosabers-AOTC.png|thumb|left|200px|Anakin Skywalker briefly wielded two lightsabers against Count Dooku]]
As a Padawan, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] studied Ataru briefly, as it fit his flashy, bold, and aggressive personality&mdash;he would later use those same traits to become a true master of [[Form V/Legends|Form V]]. Anakin applied the two-lightsaber variant of Ataru against Darth Tyranus on Geonosis during the Battle of Geonosis. Because neither Ataru nor dual-wielding were Skywalker's most effective styles, Tyranus broke through it easily, forcing the young Padawan to switch back to his standard Form V.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> During the Clone Wars, despite his mastery of Djem So, Anakin would prove to have advanced in his Ataru training, displaying proficiency in applying Ataru acrobatic moves and maneuvers, which he would often incorporate in his lightsaber combat,<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> and would also train [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] in Ataru.<ref name="WildSpace">''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]''</ref> After his transformation and [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|defeat]] on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], Darth Vader included elements of Form IV in his personalized variation of [[Form V/Legends|Form V]],<ref name="Dark Lord: Rise of Darth Vader">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> such as during his second duel with Jedi Master [[Roan Shryne]].<ref name="The Last of the Jedi: Secret Weapon">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Secret Weapon]]''</ref> While at first the cumbersome weight of his armor made it considerably difficult for him to employ Ataru acrobatics, as he regained some of his old agility through extensive training, he regained full capability in applying such maneuvers, although he only applied it when pushed. He would train his [[Galen Marek|secret apprentice]] in Ataru as well, resulting in Marek's familiarity with Ataru, and Marek's personal droid [[PROXY]] attempted to emulate the form with a combat module based on the capabilities of Qui-Gon Jinn, though while its aggression and agility was incredible, without the aid of the Force, which the apprentice found to be a notable weakness, Marek didn't have much difficulty overcoming it, though he was impressed with PROXY's competent usage of Ataru anyway.<ref name="TFU" /> The usage by the apprentice was displayed in both single- and dual-saber variants.<ref name="TFU" /><ref name="TFU II">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]</ref>

Circa [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], Jedi Padawans were discouraged from practicing Ataru, as their youthful energy was considered prone to sloppy execution of its cadences.<ref name="TJP" /> However, by the waning years of the Old Republic, Padawans would spend a year or two studying each Form from II to V, including Ataru.<ref name="EGTTF" />

[[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] Jedi [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]]<ref name="SoraDatabank">{{DB|character|sorabulq|Bulq, Sora}}</ref> as well as [[Lannik (species)/Legends|Lannik]] Jedi Master [[Even Piell/Legends|Even Piell]] had also mastered Ataru, in addition to other saber forms.<ref name="Jedi Twilight">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref> Piell's apprentice, [[Jax Pavan]], also learned Ataru, along with the other forms, during his [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]].<ref name="Patterns of Force">''[[Coruscant Nights III: Patterns of Force]]''</ref> [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]] Jedi Master [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] was another competent practitioner of Form IV,<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> often incorporating its acrobatics.<ref name="Republic 66">[[Republic 66|''Republic'' 66]]</ref>

The [[New Jedi Order]] learned of this form, along with the others, from the book ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]'',<ref name="TJP" /> [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]], and recordings, particularly the [[Great Holocron/Legends|Great Holocron]], which included a recording by Cin Drallig explaining lightsaber forms.<ref name="EGTTF" /> [[Kyle Katarn]]<ref name="LotF Preview 5">Based on statements in {{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/LOTFpreview5|text=''Legacy of the Force'' Preview 5: Darth Krayt and Kyle Katarn, Jedi Battlemaster}}</ref> and Jedi Knight [[Alema Rar]], among others, were trained in the fourth form of lightsaber combat.<ref name="Fury" /> Grand Master [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] also had knowledge and skill in the use of Ataru, as did his wife, [[Mara Jade Skywalker]].<ref name="JATM" /> Skywalker learned the form from Yoda and passed it on to his students, teaching them to embrace it not as a weapon of first use and to use both their weapon and their body in practicing Ataru.<ref name="Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 1" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Yoda_soulcaliber4.jpg|thumb|right|125px|Yoda's non-canon Form IV usage in ''[[Soulcalibur IV]]'']]
Ataru, along with forms II, III, and VII was first mentioned in ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]'', but little information was given about the form other than a brief description of it, and listing Anakin Skywalker as a known practitioner.<ref name="AotC VD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Along with the other six classical forms, it was fully fleshed out and described by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]] in ''[[Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat]]'' after the release of ''Episode II'', as part of [[Star Wars Insider 62|''Star Wars Insider'' 62]]. Reynolds was aided in this work by fencer Jack "Stelen" Bobo.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" />

In the [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]], ''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]'', and ''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]'', ''Ataru'' is misspelled as ''Ataro''. ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]'' mentions "the Jedi lightsaber style known as Ataru, in which deflection is prized above aggression." This statement contradicts Ataru's form, as it is not very good for deflecting blaster bolts and is one of the most aggressive of the seven forms. The dictionary likely intends to refer to [[Form III/Legends|Form III]] instead.

Ataru, along with the other lightsaber forms, appears in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' as part of moves and techniques employable by Jedi characters. This has not definitively been deemed canonical.<ref name="SonyCite-Jedi Abilities: Learning the Way">{{SonyCite|url=en_US/players/content.vm?id=66843&resource=features|text=Jedi Abilities: Learning the Way}}</ref> It is possible that the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] was trained in the use of Form IV after her return from exile. However, it is also possible that she was a [[Jedi Consular]] and learned the Force forms instead.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" />

In ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', Ataru is the form of choice for the Combat specialization available to [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|Jedi Sentinels]], as well as the Carnage specialization available to [[Sith Marauder]]s. Both of those specializations focus on speed over strength and the quantity of strikes over their quality. The form itself is only a passive ability and does not cause any visual changes in the fighting style.

Ataru has a [[Canon|non-canonical]] appearance as part of Yoda's inclusion in the fighting game ''[[Soulcalibur IV]]'', as Yoda wields Ataru in combat against other characters.<ref name="Soul Calibur IV">''[[Soulcalibur IV]]''</ref><ref name="SW.com Fightsaber">{{SWArchive|url=games/videogames/news20080728.html|text=Fightsaber: Mastering the Art of Lightsaber Combat}}</ref>
